inputs.model.prompt:
Create ONE landscape animal reference sheet showing the SAME individual
grey-brown tabby cat in exactly SIX full-body views, arranged as THREE COLUMNS
and TWO ROWS with clear whitespace and no printed labels or divider lines.
Read the layout left to right:
TOP ROW: standing FRONT; standing LEFT THREE-QUARTER; standing TRUE LEFT PROFILE.
BOTTOM ROW: standing BACK; SITTING LEFT THREE-QUARTER; LYING LEFT THREE-QUARTER.
One cat repeated six times as reference views, not six different individuals.
Do not add any other animal, human, accessory or inset.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 is the cat identity source. Preserve this cat's natural adult
proportions, grey-brown short fur with its visible dark tabby stripes, forehead
and cheek markings, pointed ears, whiskers, lighter muzzle/chin area, striped
legs and ringed tail with the darker tip as seen. Tabby is a coat pattern, not
a newly assigned breed. Keep the eyes' appearance consistent with the source
without introducing a newly specified precise colour. Do not invent a name,
sex, exact measurements, new patches, collar or jewellery. Ignore all furniture,
rug, room lighting and the grey rectangle in that crop: the rectangle is only
non-target background cleanup, not part of the cat or its graphic design.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 is a GRAPHIC STYLE reference ONLY, the approved illustrated
adult portrait. Borrow its fine visible dark contours, painterly cel shadow
facets, restrained surface detail and realistic-proportion semi-anime language.
DO NOT depict the man, his face, hair, body, suit or room, and do not make the
cat human-faced or anthropomorphic. Harmonize the cat gently toward this drawn
style: simplify individual fur strokes and group shadows while retaining the
distinctive stripes, silhouette and natural feline anatomy from image 1.
Not a photograph, plastic 3D render, chibi, oversized-eyed mascot or fantasy cat.

In the standing front view face the viewer on four naturally placed paws.
In the left three-quarter views show the anatomical left side and turn the nose
toward image-left. The TRUE LEFT PROFILE must show the ENTIRE body side-on:
head, shoulders, ribcage, pelvis, legs and paws all lateral, nose toward image-left;
not just a sideways head on a three-quarter chest. In BACK face away naturally.
SITTING is an ordinary resting seated cat with natural hindquarters and front
paws; LYING is a relaxed cat resting on its underside with the paws placed
naturally. Four anatomically correct legs/paws per cat, allowing normal far-limb
occlusion, no extra or fused limbs, and no standing on human-like hind legs.

Keep the SAME body scale and proportions across all six views: seated and
lying poses naturally have different extents, do not enlarge them to fill
their cells. Include the complete visible head, ears, whiskers, paws and tail
within each cell with comfortable margins. No cut-off tails, overlapping views,
distorted body length or duplicated paws. Maintain the same markings where
comparable; unseen-side markings are restrained plausible completions, not
permission to change this individual's coat or add an extravagant new pattern.

Plain neutral-grey comparison background, soft diffuse even illumination
consistent across the sheet, restrained small grounding shadows and readable
fur colours and markings. Keep a subtle muted olive/charcoal painted-shadow
sensibility without tinting the entire cat green. No amber nocturnal rim light,
dramatic black shadows, living-room scene, furniture, props, floor plan, text,
names, labels, panel borders, layout lines or watermark.
